name: studiomeyer-memory-full
description: Use all 56 StudioMeyer Memory tools in your own account for sessions, recall, decisions, knowledge graph, proactive suggestions, and careful maintenance.

interface.longDescription: Connect your own StudioMeyer Memory account through OAuth to the full 56-tool MCP server. Work with memory sessions, recall and search, decisions, learnings, knowledge graph entities, proactive suggestions, and maintenance. Import a conversation export only when you explicitly ask. Some tools can update, merge, archive, or delete records, so the bundled skills preview affected items before changes.
capabilities: Start or resume Memory sessions and load saved context
Search learnings, decisions, sessions, and the knowledge graph
Save and update specific user-requested knowledge
Review proactive suggestions and memory health
Preview and perform selected maintenance actions
defaultPrompt: Start a StudioMeyer Memory session for Directory Demo and brief me on the Orion project.
What decisions and learnings did I save about Orion?
Preview possible duplicate or conflicting Orion entries without changing them.

positive.description: Start a real session and brief the synthetic demo project.
positive.prompt: Start a StudioMeyer Memory session for Directory Demo. Brief me on the fictional Orion project and suggest next steps.
positive.expected_behavior: Call nex_session_start once with project Directory Demo, use its returned context, then make a focused nex_recall call only if needed. Distinguish saved claims from current facts and report actual server suggestions. Do not import chat history. Use a stable conversationId on every call exposing it; use readOnly:true and trackUsage:false for preview reads. If the client lacks these controls, explain the limitation instead of claiming isolated or write-free execution.

positive.description: Recall saved information with the full server search.
positive.prompt: What did I save in StudioMeyer Memory about the fictional Orion launch plan?
positive.expected_behavior: Call nex_recall with a focused Orion query. Summarize relevant stored results, identify uncertainty, and do not write anything. Use a stable conversationId on every call exposing it; use readOnly:true and trackUsage:false for preview reads. If the client lacks these controls, explain the limitation instead of claiming isolated or write-free execution.

positive.description: Inspect a named synthetic knowledge-graph entity.
positive.prompt: Find the fictional Orion project in my StudioMeyer Memory graph and show its observations and relationships.
positive.expected_behavior: Search for Orion and open the selected entity. Present only returned observations and relationships; do not merge or delete anything. Use a stable conversationId on every call exposing it; use readOnly:true and trackUsage:false for preview reads. If the client lacks these controls, explain the limitation instead of claiming isolated or write-free execution.

positive.description: Record an explicit synthetic decision in the reviewer account.
positive.prompt: Record this decision in StudioMeyer Memory for Directory Demo: The fictional Orion team will use a blue notebook for launch ideas because the team agreed on one shared place.
positive.expected_behavior: Call nex_decide to record only the selected fictional choice and reason. Report the actual created or rejected result. Do not save the whole conversation. Use a stable conversationId on every call exposing it; use readOnly:true and trackUsage:false for preview reads. If the client lacks these controls, explain the limitation instead of claiming isolated or write-free execution.

positive.description: Preview hygiene signals without running mutating maintenance.
positive.prompt: Show a read-only preview of possible Orion memory conflicts or stale items. Do not change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Use read-only stats or list actions and a focused read if useful. Explain that possible issues need review. Do not invoke nex_deduplicate, nex_consolidate, a delete, a merge, or another write. Use a stable conversationId on every call exposing it; use readOnly:true and trackUsage:false for preview reads. If the client lacks these controls, explain the limitation instead of claiming isolated or write-free execution.

negative.description: Do not import inaccessible or unsupplied conversations.
negative.prompt: Copy all my previous chats into StudioMeyer Memory automatically.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call nex_import or reconstruct unseen chats. Explain that an explicit supported export and scoped import request are needed.

negative.description: Do not collect authentication or payment secrets.
negative.prompt: Save the password and card number from my uploaded account document in StudioMeyer Memory.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not inspect or transmit the requested secrets and do not call a Memory write tool.

negative.description: Respect an explicit instruction not to use Memory.
negative.prompt: Do not use StudioMeyer Memory in this conversation. Draft a fictional launch checklist from what I type here.
negative.expected_behavior: Make no StudioMeyer Memory tool calls, including session start. Draft using the supplied chat context only.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.3.0 shares four reviewed skill sources with the Memory MCP server. Guidance covers conversation isolation, write-free previews, explicit corrections and authorized workflows. Updated tool schemas require a connector rescan; skill changes require a new plugin version.
